questions.prompt: What is Anthropic's "golden rule" for checking a prompt?

options.text: Make the prompt as short as possible, so the model has fewer words it could misread.
options.explanation: Short is not the test. A short prompt that leaves out the goal still confuses the model.

options.text: Show it to a colleague with little context; if they'd be confused, the model will be too.
options.explanation: Right. The model starts with no context about your team, just like a new colleague.

options.text: Use one standard prompt for every task, so the results of the whole team stay the same each time.
options.explanation: Each task needs its own goal, context, constraints and format.

questions.prompt: You paste a 40-page report and want one answer from it. Where should your question go?

options.text: At the end, after the report.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's and Gemini's guides both say: long context first, the question at the end.

options.text: At the start, before the report.
options.explanation: For long documents, both guides recommend the opposite: the document first, the question last.

options.text: It does not matter where it goes.
options.explanation: Anthropic's guide says a question at the end can improve quality by up to 30 percent in tests.

questions.prompt: Why add the reason behind an instruction, for example "this will be read aloud, so avoid symbols"?

options.text: It makes the prompt longer, and longer prompts always give the model better answers in every case.
options.explanation: Length alone does not help. The reason helps because it carries information about your goal.

options.text: It helps the model understand your goal and apply the rule to cases you did not list.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's guide says context or motivation behind an instruction can help the model understand your goals.

options.text: Models ignore any instruction that does not come with a reason attached to it.
options.explanation: Models follow plain instructions too. The reason makes the result better targeted.
